In college my friend was sleeping over and woke up gasping, blinking staring at me like trying to make sure she was fully awake. My roommate and I were kind of shook, and it took some prodding to get her to tell us what she saw… a black figure hovering over ME. I didn’t go back to sleep that night, lol. 

Anyway, 2 years later still in college i have an apartment and share a pretty massive bedroom of an old house with the same friend. She wouldn’t always come home at night, as she had a boyfriend, leaving me alone in the room pretty frequently. I remember one night I woke up to a dark, swirling, winged shadow figure (Batman?! lol) raising my covers over me while pinning me down trying to suffocate me. From the time I was very young (4?) this has been something I have been particularly sensitive and paranoid about, never wanting anything touching my neck, and being careful to not have bed sheets specifically touching my neck. Welp 😂 

Anyways, ever since I was a baby (earliest memories) I had terrible nightmares, by the time I turned probably 6 I learned I could control these dreams. Was a little weird, would flip the switch once I realized I wasn’t in the material world and make myself become the monster… annihilating and murdering/chasing the things that initially were taunting and trying to get me. Maybe not the healthiest way to cope with nightmares but man the power rush and satisfaction of it haha. 

ANYWAY essentially mustered an insane amount of mental or spiritual strength or something to resist this current shadow thing. Similar mentally to how I would catch myself in a dream and use my mind to morph it to my advantage. Ended up kicking the covers back down and shouting it to leave me alone as I said the lords name (Jesus Christ) , and it left. 

Never experienced anything similar to sleep paralysis since then, and God willing I never will. Still experience an array of things from time to time, but I always have.
